title: How To Not Quit Teaching
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Citing the alarming statistic that four in ten new teachers leave within five years, Linsin argues most of the dissatisfaction driving attrition is within a teacher's control, even though teacher-preparation programs and districts share systemic blame. He offers three remedies: becoming an expert in classroom management, which he calls the single most important lever for confidence, reduced stress, and satisfaction; learning to say no to optional committees, unnecessary hand-holding, and after-hours obligations; and deliberately taking care of physical and personal well-being through diet, exercise, sleep, and time away from school-related thinking. He frames the piece as a call to reject the martyrdom culture of teaching and to fight deliberately for a sustainable, long-term career.
points: Opens with the statistic that four of ten new teachers leave the profession within five years, calling it staggering and largely preventable.
Names becoming an expert in classroom management as the single most important lever for reducing stress and increasing satisfaction.
Recommends learning to say no to optional committees, unnecessary hand-holding, and non-required obligations to reclaim time.
Advises deliberate self-care — diet, exercise, sleep, and time completely away from school thinking — citing high teacher stress statistics.
Rejects the culture of teacher martyrdom, framing sustainable careers as achievable through fighting for boundaries, not sacrifice.
quotes: Four of every ten new teachers leave the profession within five years.
